benefits.name: Disabled Veteran Property Tax Exemption (Clause 22 Series)
benefits.description: Massachusetts offers a tiered set of local property tax exemptions for veterans under G.L. c. 59, §5, Clause 22 and its sub-clauses. Clause 22 grants a base exemption ($2,000 of assessed valuation or $400, whichever produces the greater abatement) to veterans with at least a 10% VA/service disability rating. Higher sub-clauses grant larger exemptions for more severe conditions: Clause 22A ($4,000/$750) for loss of use of one hand/foot or one eye, Congressional Medal of Honor recipients, or former POWs; Clause 22B ($8,000/$1,250) for loss of use of both hands/feet or both eyes; Clause 22C ($10,000/$1,500) for permanent and total disability with VA specially-adapted-housing assistance; Clause 22E ($6,000/$1,000) for a 100% VA disability rating; and Clause 22F (full exemption of the single-family-dwelling portion) for paraplegic veterans or veterans with service-connected blindness. Clause 22D provides a full exemption for surviving spouses of veterans who died of a service-connected cause or are presumptively deceased while missing in action. The statute also allows municipalities to adopt local-option increases (Clauses 22I/22J, e.g. annual CPI adjustments or additional percentage increases); this research file does not itemize each municipality's local-option amounts.
benefits.value: Ranges from $400 minimum exemption (10%+ disability, Clause 22) up to a full property tax exemption on the dwelling (100% disabled/blind or paraplegic veterans, Clause 22E/22F); exact amount depends on which sub-clause applies and any local-option increase

otherReqs: Honorable discharge
Domiciled in Massachusetts at least 6 months before entering service, OR resided in Massachusetts for 2 consecutive years before filing
Must own and occupy the property
Filed locally with the municipal Board of Assessors, not at the state level

application.agency: Massachusetts municipal Boards of Assessors (statute administered under G.L. c. 59)
documentation: DD-214 or other proof of honorable discharge

benefits.name: Massachusetts Veterans' Homes (Chelsea and Holyoke)
benefits.description: Massachusetts operates state-run veterans' homes, historically known as the Soldiers' Homes, in Chelsea (opened 1882) and Holyoke (opened 1952), providing skilled nursing, hospice, and long-term residential care to eligible veterans. Under M.G.L. c. 115A, §1, a person who meets the definition of 'veteran' in c. 115, §1 is entitled to outpatient treatment, admission, and hospitalization at a state-operated veterans' home, subject to exclusions listed in c. 115A, §3 — this session could not independently confirm the specific text of those §3 exclusions or current facility-level admission/capacity details, because mass.gov's Chelsea/Holyoke facility pages returned HTTP 403 to automated fetch. Public reporting indicates the Chelsea facility was rebuilt and reopened in 2023 and a new Holyoke facility (part of a reported $482 million state investment) was under construction as of this research; those specifics are noted for awareness and were not independently verified against a directly-read official source this session.
benefits.value: Skilled nursing, hospice, and long-term residential care at state-operated veterans' homes

otherReqs: Must meet the definition of 'veteran' under M.G.L. c. 115, §1
Subject to exclusions listed in M.G.L. c. 115A, §3 (not independently confirmed this session)
Meets medical/admission criteria set by the home

application.agency: Massachusetts Department of Veterans' Services / Office of Veterans' Homes and Housing
documentation: DD-214 or other proof of military service

benefits.name: Veterans Tuition Waiver at Massachusetts Public Colleges
benefits.description: M.G.L. c. 15A, §19 directs the Board of Higher Education to establish guidelines providing full or partial tuition waivers for designated categories of students — which may include veterans — in state-supported undergraduate degree or certificate programs at Massachusetts public colleges and universities. The statute text itself does not specify veteran-specific eligibility criteria, exact waiver amounts, or a residency requirement; it delegates 'institutional waiver allocation formulas and eligibility requirements, including needs criteria' to the Board's implementing guidelines, which this session could not independently fetch (mass.gov guideline pages returned 403). Widely repeated secondary guidance describes the program as awarding waivers on a space-available basis to Massachusetts-resident veterans not in default on federal student loans, and separately gives National Guard members a full tuition-and-fee waiver — those specific criteria are noted for awareness but were not independently re-confirmed against a directly-read official source this session.
benefits.value: Full or partial tuition waiver, awarded on a space-available basis; exact amount and criteria set by Board of Higher Education / institutional guidelines, not by the statute itself

otherReqs: Enrollment in a state-supported undergraduate degree or certificate program at a Massachusetts public college/university
Waiver granted on a space-available basis per institutional guidelines
Not in default on federal student loans (per secondary guidance, not independently re-confirmed this session)

application.agency: Massachusetts Department of Higher Education / individual public college veterans' representative

benefits.name: Civil Service Absolute Veterans' Preference
benefits.description: Massachusetts uses an absolute preference system in civil service hiring: names on open-competitive eligible lists are ranked with disabled veterans first, then other veterans, then widows or widowed mothers of veterans killed in action or who died of a service-connected disability incurred in wartime service, then all other applicants — each group internally ordered by exam standing. In the labor service, veterans are placed ahead of all other applicants on the register, and 'a disabled veteran shall be retained in employment in preference to all other persons, including veterans' during reductions in force. This is a position-based ranking preference rather than a fixed numeric point add-on to the exam score; some secondary (non-.gov) sources describe Massachusetts veterans as receiving '2 points added' to their score, but that specific point figure does not appear in the text of M.G.L. c. 31, §26 read this session, so it is not stated here as confirmed fact.
benefits.value: Absolute hiring/retention preference via ranking position on civil service eligible lists (a placement preference, not a confirmed fixed point value, per the statute text read this session)

otherReqs: Qualifying veteran status under M.G.L. c. 4, §7, cl. 43
Disabled veterans and Congressional Medal of Honor/Distinguished Service Medal/Silver Star recipients receive additional standing

application.agency: Massachusetts Human Resources Division, Civil Service Unit
documentation: VA disability rating letter (for the disabled-veteran preference tier)

benefits.name: Veteran and Purple Heart License Plates
benefits.description: The RMV issues a distinctive 'VETERAN' registration plate for an additional annual $20 fee on top of the standard registration fee, and a free 'ORDER OF THE PURPLE HEART RECIPIENT' / 'COMBAT WOUNDED' plate for one private passenger vehicle owned and principally used by a documented Purple Heart recipient (a surviving spouse may retain the plate for personal use by paying the standard registration fee plus the $20 annual fee, until remarriage or non-renewal). Massachusetts also offers a separate 'Disabled Veteran' plate reportedly tied to a 60%-or-greater VA disability rating plus qualifying disabled-parking eligibility, per RMV guidance; that specific 60% threshold and its governing statute section could not be independently confirmed this session because mass.gov's RMV pages returned HTTP 403 to automated fetch, so it is noted for awareness rather than treated as confirmed fact.
benefits.value: 'VETERAN' plate available for $20/year in addition to standard registration; Purple Heart plate issued free for one vehicle; a separate Disabled Veteran plate program exists but its exact criteria are unconfirmed this session

otherReqs: Massachusetts vehicle registration
Purple Heart plate requires documented Purple Heart award
Disabled Veteran plate program's exact disability-rating threshold not independently confirmed this session

documentation: Purple Heart award documentation (for the Purple Heart plate)
VA disability rating letter (for the Disabled Veteran plate, unconfirmed threshold)

benefits.name: Motor Vehicle Excise Tax and Sales Tax Exemptions for Disabled Veterans
benefits.description: Massachusetts exempts one motor vehicle owned and registered for a disabled veteran's personal, noncommercial use from the annual local motor vehicle excise tax if the veteran has a VA combined service-connected disability rating of 100%, is deemed individually unemployable due to a service-connected disability, or has suffered specified losses (one or both feet, one or both hands, or qualifying vision loss). A related sales tax exemption (M.G.L. c. 64H, §6(u)) applies to the purchase of one motor vehicle by a veteran who has suffered permanent loss of use of both legs, both arms, or one leg and one arm, or who has been determined permanently disabled by the medical advisory board under c. 90, §8C and issued a Disabled Veteran or Purple Heart plate. Both exemptions are limited to a single vehicle used for personal, noncommercial purposes.
benefits.value: Full exemption from annual motor vehicle excise tax on one vehicle; sales tax exemption on the purchase of one vehicle for qualifying severely disabled veterans

otherReqs: Vehicle must be owned/registered (or leased) for personal, noncommercial use
Limited to one motor vehicle

Alternate, non-percentage eligibility paths also qualify: loss/permanent loss of use of one or both feet, one or both hands, or qualifying vision loss (excise); loss of use of both legs, both arms, or one leg and one arm, or a medical-advisory-board permanent disability determination (sales tax)

application.agency: Massachusetts Department of Revenue / local Board of Assessors (excise tax); Massachusetts DOR (sales tax)
documentation: VA disability rating letter or certificate

benefits.name: Free Sporting/Hunting/Fishing License for Paraplegic Residents
benefits.description: Massachusetts law exempts paraplegic residents (and, with reciprocity, paraplegic nonresidents) from the fee for a sporting, hunting, or fishing license. This is a disability-based exemption under M.G.L. c. 131, §11 rather than a veteran-specific benefit — the statute text read this session makes no separate mention of veterans or VA disability ratings — so it applies to any qualifying paraplegic resident, which in practice includes many severely disabled veterans but is not limited to them. A 2025-2026 legislative proposal (referenced in search results as H.3481) would reportedly extend a no-cost hunting/fishing license specifically to 100% disabled veterans regardless of the paraplegic criterion; that bill's text and enactment status were not fetched or confirmed this session and should not be treated as current law.
benefits.value: Free sporting, hunting, and fishing license for qualifying paraplegic residents

otherReqs: Must meet the statutory definition of paraplegic
Nonresident paraplegics qualify only if their home state offers reciprocal free licensing to Massachusetts residents

application.agency: Massachusetts Division of Fisheries and Wildlife (MassWildlife)

benefits.name: Annuity for Severely Disabled Veterans
benefits.description: Massachusetts pays a $2,500 annual annuity, in one payment on August 1, to a veteran who has lost both legs, or who has been determined 100% disabled by the VA as a result of enemy action or an accident certified by the VA to be service-connected. Evidence of the qualifying service and disability must be submitted to and certified by the Secretary of Veterans' Services under c. 115, §6C before the Comptroller pays the annuity. This is distinct from — and narrower than — the broader, means-tested Chapter 115 'Veterans' Benefits' program (G.L. c. 115) that provides need-based monthly cash assistance to low-income veterans and their dependents for food, shelter, clothing, and other essentials; this session confirmed that broader program's existence and its city/town-reimbursement mechanism (the Commonwealth reimburses 75% of municipal Chapter 115 expenditures) via a direct read of the statute, but could not independently confirm the current monthly benefit formula or cap for individual applicants against a directly-read official source, because mass.gov's Chapter 115 program page returned HTTP 403 — so no per-applicant dollar figure for the general Chapter 115 program is stated here.
benefits.value: $2,500 annual annuity (single payment, August 1) for qualifying severely disabled veterans; separately, a means-tested monthly cash-assistance program (Chapter 115) exists but its current benefit amounts are not confirmed here

otherReqs: Loss of both legs, OR VA-certified 100% disability resulting from enemy action or a service-connected accident
Evidence certified by the Secretary of Veterans' Services per M.G.L. c. 115, §6C

application.agency: Massachusetts Department of Veterans' Services / Office of the Comptroller
documentation: VA certification of service-connected 100% disability or loss of both legs

benefits.name: State Income Tax Exemption for VA Disability Compensation and Military Pensions
benefits.description: Massachusetts does not tax veterans' disability pensions, VA disability compensation, or G.I. benefits. Per the Commonwealth's own FY2026 Tax Expenditure Budget, this exemption is mandated by federal law (38 U.S.C. §5301), which preempts state taxation of these amounts — it is a federally-required exclusion, not a discretionary state tax break, and the state's own budget document estimates it reduces Massachusetts personal income tax revenue by approximately $69.5 million in FY2026. Secondary (non-.gov) sources also state that Massachusetts does not tax military retirement/noncontributory pension income from the U.S. uniformed services; that specific claim about military retirement pay could not be independently confirmed against a directly-read official Massachusetts Department of Revenue source this session (DOR guidance pages returned 403), so it is noted for awareness rather than treated as equally confirmed alongside the VA-compensation exemption, which the state's own official budget document does confirm.
benefits.value: Full exemption from Massachusetts personal income tax for VA disability compensation, disability pensions, and G.I. benefits (federally mandated); a parallel exemption for military retirement pay is reported but not independently re-confirmed this session

otherReqs: Applies automatically to qualifying federal veterans' disability/pension/G.I. benefit income; no separate state application required

documentation: Not applicable — exemption applies automatically to qualifying federal benefit income
